newsitem.title: CANADA: Cambridge sells mall stakes for C$315 mln.
newsitem.headline: Cambridge sells mall stakes for C$315 mln.

text.p: Cambridge Shopping Centres said on it agreed to sell its stake in five malls to a unit of the Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan Board for C$315 million.
The Toronto-based real estate company said it would earn C$117 million in net proceeds from the sale.
However, Cambridge said under the agreement it will use C$65 million of the proceeds to buy back one of the malls from Ivanhoe III Inc of Montreal, a third party involved in the transaction.

Under the agreement, Cambridge will sell its interests in the Chinook Centre in Calgary, Intercity Shopping Centre in Thunder Bay, New Sudbury Centre in Sudbury, Markville Shopping Centre in Markham and Bayshore Shopping Centre in Ottawa to Ontrea Inc. Ontrea is a unit of the Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan.
Cambridge and Ontrea jointly own the first four malls, while the Bayshore Shopping Centre is jointly owned by Cambridge, Ontrea and Ivanhoe.

Ivanhoe will now exercise its right to buy Ontrea's interest in the Bayshore Shopping Centre, then sell the entire mall to Cambridge for C$65 million, Cambridge said. The company said the transaction would leave it about C$50 million for other investment opportunities.

"The acquisition of this market-dominant property (Bayshore) is an example of how we intend to use proceeds from the sale to Ontrea, and since Ottawa is a strategically important region, we are increasing our investment there," Cambridge chief executive Lorne Braithwaite said in a statement.
Cambridge said the initial financial impact of the transactions on its operating results was expected to be marginally positive.

Due to the acquisition of stakes in five other shopping centers completed earlier this fiscal year, the total square footage owned by Cambridge will be about the same as last year following the transactions, the company said.
